drivingQuestion: After the second festival day, may one use what a gentile cut on it immediately, or must one wait בכדי שיעשו?
outcomeNote: Rava rules that one must wait בכדי שיעשו, as Rav Shemaya argued

segments.he: הָנְהוּ בְּנֵי גְנָנָא דְּגַזּוּ לְהוּ אָסָא בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי, לְאוּרְתָּא שְׁרָא לְהוּ רָבִינָא לְאוֹרוֹחֵי בֵּיהּ לְאַלְתַּר. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא לְרָבִינָא: לֵיסַר לְהוּ מָר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵינָן בְּנֵי תוֹרָה.
segments.en: The Gemara relates that «certain canopy makers,» who would braid myrtle branches into their canopies, once «cut myrtles on the second day of a Festival,» and «in the evening Ravina permitted» people «to smell them immediately» at the conclusion of the Festival. «Rava bar Taḥalifa said to Ravina: The Master should prohibit them» to do this, «as they are not knowledgeable in Torah,» and therefore we should be stringent with them lest they come to treat the sanctity of the second Festival day lightly.

segments.he: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שְׁמַעְיָה: טַעְמָא דְּאֵינָן בְּנֵי תוֹרָה, הָא בְּנֵי תוֹרָה שְׁרֵי?! וְהָא בָּעִינַן בִּכְדֵי שֶׁיֵּעָשׂוּ! אֲזַלוּ שַׁיְילוּהּ לְרָבָא, אֲמַר לְהוּ: בָּעִינַן בִּכְדֵי שֶׁיֵּעָשׂוּ.
segments.en: «Rav Shemaya strongly objects to this: The reason» given here is «that they are not knowledgeable in Torah;» but if «they were knowledgeable in Torah, would it be permitted? Don’t we require» them to wait «the time needed for» the myrtle’s «preparation,» i.e., the time it takes to cut them? «They went and asked Rava. He said to them: We require» them to wait «the time needed for» the myrtle’s «preparation.»
